reviews.title: Incredible performance from SteelSeries
reviews.comment:
These headphones completely blew my expectations out of the water.  I'd been previously using open ear headphones and a standalone mic for gaming, but got tired of fiddling with the mic and moving it around my desk, just for people to struggle to hear me.  I also was getting tired of wires, so enter the wireless Artis Nova 5.
Wireless Performance is absolutely fantastic.  With the 2.4 ghz dongle I never have connection issues.  Battery life has performed better than expected.  I typically only charge them after 20 hrs or so of gaming, so it's basically an afterthought.
Sound quality is also better than I expected.  The good news is it's completely customizable via SteelSeries EQ software either on your phone or desktop, so you can tailor the sound and clarity to your exact application.
Quality of the headset is fantastic.  I would be somewhat careful with them, as you should with any lightweight headset, but they seem very durable for daily use.  I've never had any issues after over a month or use.
reviews.author: Cody

reviews.title: Finally Found a Wireless Headset That Replaces My A40s
reviews.comment:
I’ve bought several wired and wireless headsets trying to replace my old Astro A40 Gen 1s. Those things have incredible sound and mic quality and have lasted forever with nothing but new ear pads and a new cord. But I’m tired of having a wire running across my desk, so I started hunting for a true wireless replacement.
I tried a bunch of headsets: some wired, some wireless from big-name brands, and while the sound quality was usually good, the microphones always fell short. Almost every pair I tested had the same complaint: “The mic isn’t clear,” or “you sound far away.” I ended up returning all of them. I even went through Reddit threads, YouTube mic tests, and a dozen “Top 10 Headsets” lists. I compared those recommendations to Amazon reviews, where even 4- and 5-star headsets often have tons of comments saying the mic is garbage.
After watching real mic test videos, I decided to try this headset,  and I think I finally found the one.
The features are exactly what I wanted. It’s wireless, and it works with pretty much anything thanks to the Bluetooth and 2.4GHz dongle options. Switching between them is literally a tap of a button. The comfort band on top is a huge upgrade over stiff foam padding and keeps pressure off my head, so no headaches. And the microphone hiding inside the earcup? Genuinely awesome. It stays protected, doesn’t stick out awkwardly, and pulls out smoothly when needed.
Controls are easy: a volume dial, a one-tap mute button, and a power button that only needs a couple seconds of holding. The basics are done right.
Sound quality is great for both music and games,  solid bass, clear mids and highs, and overall it sounds more like using my desktop speakers than a typical gaming headset. The real test, though, is the microphone. I hopped on Discord and asked the same question I’ve asked with every other headset: “Can you hear me, and do I sound clear?” For the first time in a long time, I got: “Yes, you sound like you always do.” Finally. Check.
On top of that, the software gives you a ton of customization. You can choose presets, adjust EQ, tweak mic quality, and personalize everything from desktop, web, or mobile. It’s a lot more than I expected at this price.
Battery life hasn’t been an issue at all. I haven’t charged it once in five straight days of use, including multiple gaming sessions each day. Even if it needed charging, that wouldn’t bother me because everything else checks out.
For me, this headset hits every key point I care about. It’s not even at a premium price, but it performs like something that should be. Definitely do your research, because a lot of premium-name headsets have great sound but fall short in the mic department. This one finally delivers on both.
reviews.author: Mr. E

reviews.title: Great Battery Life and Solid All-Around Performance
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 Wireless for a bit now, and it’s turned out to be a really well-rounded headset—especially if you switch between different systems.
The biggest highlight for me is the versatility. It works across PC, PlayStation, Switch, and even mobile pretty seamlessly thanks to the USB-C dongle and Bluetooth. Switching between devices is easy, although you do have to toggle between them rather than using both at once.
Sound quality is solid overall. It’s not ultra-premium, but it’s clear and balanced enough for both gaming and casual music. The companion app with tons of audio presets is actually useful—you can tweak the sound depending on what you’re playing, which adds a nice layer of customization.
Battery life is honestly one of the best parts. It lasts a long time—I rarely worry about charging it—and even a quick charge gives you hours of use. It’s rated up to around 60 hours, which feels pretty accurate in real use.
Comfort is also typical SteelSeries—lightweight with a snug fit that works well for long sessions. That said, the earcups might feel a bit small if you have larger ears, which is something a few users have pointed out.
The microphone is better than expected. Voice comes through clearly for chat, and background noise is handled pretty well, making it solid for multiplayer or calls.
On the downside, it doesn’t have some premium features like active noise cancellation (on all versions), and it’s not meant to replace higher-end audiophile headsets. But for the price range, it hits a really nice balance.
Overall, this is a great mid-range wireless gaming headset. It’s comfortable, flexible across platforms, and packed with useful features without being overly complicated—definitely a strong choice for everyday gaming
